High-Mileage 2023 Corvette Z06 Coupe 3LZ Fails To Find a Buyer for $85,000
16 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
You guys already know I'm a big believer in buying used Z06s of the C8 variety, especially now that prices have come down considerably compared to what people were paying a few years ago. However, there are a few things I wouldn't compromise on when it comes to supercars, and accident history is definitely one of them.
Take this 2023 Z06 Coupe 3LZ for instance - recently up for grabs at auction where the bidding stopped at $85,000, falling short of the reserve. The seller called the result "close", which means they were probably expecting around $90,000? At least, that would be my guess.
But here's the thing. Not only does this car have 24,000 miles on the odometer, it also has a "dirty" Carfax report, which lists damage to the front, left side, and left front corner. It's tough to gauge the full extent of the damage, and not even the selling dealer could provide us with all the necessary details. Here's what they had to say in the ad's comments section:
"We do not know exactly what happened during the accident. The car looks perfect! We have tried calling Selman Chevrolet to get more information but they refuse to provide it. The paint looks original. The bumper doesn't even look like it has been repainted and it is possible that it has not been."
"It is possible that something went through the radiator and condenser which had to be replaced, likely under insurance claim."
To be fair, the car sounds like it's in really good shape, but for $90k? You can find one with a clean Carfax for roughly that sum; maybe a few grand more. So yes, I'd rather pay another $10,000 or so for a clean example - just recently we saw a 2023 Z06 Coupe 2LZ go for $92,500 with just over 5,000 miles on the clock. That's the sweet spot.
As for this particular car, the spec isn't bad, obviously. It's got an Amplify Orange Tintcoat exterior, Jake C8.R graphics (for a motorsport-inspired vibe), LED headlights, a rear spoiler, plus a set of 20" and 21" forged wheels with Michelin tires and ventilated discs at each corner. It also comes with a front-axle lift system and Magnetic Selective Ride Control.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the Jet Black leather GT2 bucket seats (heated/ventilated/power-adjustable), a 14-speaker Bose sound system, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, the Stealth Interior Trim Package, plus your basic electronic driver aids such as rear cross-traffic alert and blind-spot monitoring.
As for performance, you already know what's up with the 5.5-liter LT6 V8 . It's sending 670 horsepower and 460 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via a Tremec TR-9080 eight-speed dual-clutch automatic. This Vette was factory-fitted with a performance exhaust system featuring driver-selectable modes.
So, what do you guys think? Was $85,000 a reasonable offer? I believe that it was. Maybe even generous (depending on the extent of the damage and the quality of the repairs). There's also some curb rash on the right-front wheel, but that's obviously only a minor concern.
